lesson_title: The Crackle in Your Jersey: Coulomb's Law
hook_text: A balloon rubbed for five seconds can beat the gravity of the entire planet. Here's the law that says so.
clip_script: Rub a balloon on your hair and stick it to the wall. Think about what just happened: a toy you charged in five seconds is holding itself up against the gravitational pull of the ENTIRE EARTH. That is how loud the electric force is. And here's the good news — you already know its formula. Gravitation: multiply the masses, divide by distance squared. Coulomb's law: multiply the CHARGES, divide by distance squared. Same skeleton. Two microcoulombs and three microcoulombs, ten centimetres apart? Convert, multiply, divide: 5,4 newtons. Opposite signs, so it's a pull. Same signs would make it a push — that's the one trick gravity never learned. Three charges in a row? Tug-of-war. The middle charge feels one force from each neighbour: draw the two arrows first — pull toward opposites, push away from likes — then add if they agree, subtract if they fight. Arrows before arithmetic, always. And when the distance doubles, the force drops to a quarter. Distance always gets squared. Crackling jersey, sticking balloon, biting doorknob — all of it obeying one line of maths.
visual_style: A balloon rubbing on hair and snapping to a wall with force arrows appearing; a split-screen showing the gravitation and Coulomb formulas morphing into each other; three charges on a line playing tug-of-war with glowing arrows.
mood: Playful and electric — static shocks turned into scoreboard points.
pacing: Snappy hook, steady formula beat, quick-fire tug-of-war finish.
